items.text: LEARNINGOBJECTIVES

items.label: list_item
items.text: Define the terms 'enthalpy change of solution, soH', and 'enthalpy change of hydration, hyaH of an ion'.

items.label: list_item
items.text: Use energy cycles and energy level diagrams to calculate the enthalpy change of solution of an ionic compound using the enthalpy change of hydration and the lattice energy

items.label: list_item
items.text: Understand the effect of ionic charge and ionic radius on the values of the enthalpy change of hydration and the lattice energy of anioniccompound.

items.label: section_header
items.text: ENTHALPYCHANGEOFSOLUTION,△SoH

items.label: text
items.text: The solubilities of ionic solids in water show a very wide variation, and there is no obvious pattern.

items.label: text
items.text: Oneofthefactorsthatdeterminessolubilityisthevalueoftheenthalpychangeofsolution, soH, the enthalpy change when one mole of anionic solid dissolves in water to form an infinitely dilute solution.

items.label: text
items.text: The enthalpy change of solutionfor sodium chloride is the energy change associated with the following process:

items.label: formula
items.text: NaCl(s) → Na⁺(aq) + Cl⁻(aq)

items.label: text
items.text: It is important to specify the extent of dilution of the final solution when quoting a value for the enthalpy change.Upon dilution,theions in the solution move further apart(an endothermic process) andalsobecomemorehydrated(anexothermicprocess).

items.label: text
items.text: Therelativeimportanceofthesetwoprocesses(endothermicandexothermic)changeswithdilution, and they affect thevalueofsoHin a complicatedway.For thisreason,thequotedvaluesforsoH refer to aninfinitelydilutesolution.Thisvalue cannot bedetermined experimentally andisfound by aprocessofextrapolation.

items.label: text
items.text: In practice, there comes a point when further dilution has no measurable effect on soH. This is known as the point of infinite dilution.

items.text: ENTHALPY CHANGE OF HYDRATION, hyaH

items.label: text
items.text: The enthalpy change of hydration, hydH, is the enthalpy change when one mole of an ion in its gaseous state is completely hydrated bywaterIn practice,completehydration is said to have occurredwhenthesolutionformedisatinfinitedilution.

items.label: text
items.text: For the sodium and chloride ions, the enthalpy change of hydration is the enthalpy change for the following processes:

items.label: text
items.text: Na+(g) aq, Na+(aq)

items.label: text
items.text: Cl-(g)  Cl-(aq)
